unit.title: Reformulation & Cohesion
unit.subtitle: Connectors that restate, specify, summarize, and digress

grammar.title: Restate and wrap up like a native
grammar.intro: A C1 speaker rarely says something once. You reformulate to clarify (es decir, o sea), you specify (a saber), you rephrase (dicho de otro modo), and you close with a summary (en definitiva, en suma). You can even step aside for a moment (por cierto). These cohesion markers let you structure an idea across several turns instead of dumping it all at once.

sections.heading: Restating: es decir, o sea, esto es
sections.body: These introduce an equivalent, clearer version of what you just said ('that is / in other words'). Es decir is neutral and works in speech and writing; esto es is more formal/written; o sea is colloquial and very frequent in speech. They are always followed by a comma.

ex.es: Llegó tarde, es decir, perdió el turno.
ex.en: He arrived late, that is, he lost his slot.
He's self-taught, in other words, he learned on his own.

sections.heading: Specifying: a saber, en otras palabras, dicho de otro modo
sections.body: Use a saber to introduce a list or precise detail ('namely'). Use en otras palabras or dicho de otro modo / de otra manera to rephrase a difficult idea in a fresh way ('put another way'). These signal that clarity, not new information, is coming.

ex.es: Faltan tres requisitos, a saber: firma, sello y fecha.
ex.en: Three requirements are missing, namely: signature, stamp and date.

ex.es: No es rentable; dicho de otro modo, perdemos dinero.
ex.en: It isn't profitable; put another way, we're losing money.

sections.heading: Summing up: en definitiva, en suma, en resumidas cuentas, en resumen
sections.body: These close and condense an argument. En resumen and en suma announce a summary ('in short'); en definitiva delivers the final verdict ('ultimately / when all's said and done'); en resumidas cuentas is the idiomatic 'to cut a long story short'. They cue the listener that the conclusion has arrived.
conj: to cut a long story short

ex.es: En definitiva, la reforma no convence a nadie.
ex.en: Ultimately, the reform convinces no one.

ex.es: En resumidas cuentas, salió más caro de lo previsto.
ex.en: To cut a long story short, it turned out pricier than expected.

sections.heading: Stepping aside: por cierto, a propósito
sections.body: Both introduce a digression — a related aside or a change of subject ('by the way'). Por cierto is the everyday marker; a propósito often introduces something the current topic reminded you of. Don't confuse the discourse marker por cierto (by the way) with the adjective phrase por cierto meaning 'for certain'.
conj: by the way / speaking of which

ex.es: Por cierto, ¿enviaste el informe que te pedí?
ex.en: By the way, did you send the report I asked for?

ex.es: A propósito de plazos, el tuyo vence mañana.
ex.en: Speaking of deadlines, yours is due tomorrow.

takeaways: Restate: es decir / o sea / esto es (that is, in other words).
Specify: a saber (namely), en otras palabras, dicho de otro modo (put another way).
Sum up: en resumen / en suma (in short), en definitiva (ultimately), en resumidas cuentas.
Digress: por cierto / a propósito (by the way).

mistakes.w: Es autodidacta, es que aprendió solo.
mistakes.r: Es autodidacta, es decir, aprendió solo.
mistakes.why: To reformulate ('that is'), use 'es decir'; 'es que' means 'the thing is' and gives a reason, not a restatement.
'En resumen' stands alone before a comma; don't append 'de todo' to it.

mistakes.w: Por cierto de los plazos, el tuyo vence mañana.
mistakes.r: A propósito de los plazos, el tuyo vence mañana.
mistakes.why: To link a digression to a topic use 'a propósito de'; 'por cierto' does not take 'de + topic'.

exercises.prompt: No es rentable; ___, estamos perdiendo dinero.
exercises.prompt_en: It isn't profitable; put another way, we're losing money.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! Reformulas la misma idea con otras palabras.
exercises.no: You're rephrasing the same idea, so use 'dicho de otro modo' (put another way), not a contrast or consequence marker.

exercises.prompt: Faltan tres documentos, ___: el contrato, la factura y el recibo.
exercises.prompt_en: Three documents are missing, namely: the contract, the invoice and the receipt.
exercises.no: To introduce a precise list use 'a saber' (namely).

exercises.prompt: Build: "Ultimately, the reform convinces no one."
exercises.no: For a final verdict use 'en definitiva' (ultimately), not the contrast marker 'en cambio'.

exercises.prompt: ___, ¿enviaste el informe que te pedí ayer?
exercises.prompt_en: By the way, did you send the report I asked you for yesterday?
exercises.hint: A two-word marker that introduces an aside: 'by the way'.
exercises.no: The everyday 'by the way' marker is 'por cierto'.

exercises.prompt: Match each connector to its discourse function.

exercises.tts: En resumidas cuentas, salió más caro de lo previsto.
accepted: en resumidas cuentas salio mas caro de lo previsto
exercises.translation: To cut a long story short, it turned out pricier than expected.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “En resumidas cuentas, salió más caro de lo previsto.”
exercises.no: It was: “En resumidas cuentas, salió más caro de lo previsto.” (To cut a long story short, it turned out pricier than expected.)

exercises.scenario: Wrapping up a long project meeting 🗂️

lines.speaker: Directora
lines.es: Hemos revisado presupuesto, plazos y riesgos. ¿Alguna conclusión?
lines.en: We've reviewed budget, timelines and risks. Any conclusion?

options.text: En suma, el proyecto es viable si ajustamos el calendario.
Por el contrario, hemos revisado presupuesto, plazos y riesgos.
A saber, no tengo ninguna conclusión que darte hoy.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! 'En suma' condensa y cierra el análisis.
exercises.no: You're asked to conclude, so open with a summary marker: 'en suma' (in sum).

exercises.say: Es decir, conviene replantear el enfoque.
exercises.en: That is, it's worth rethinking the approach.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “Es decir, conviene replantear el enfoque.”

vocab.en: to cut a long story short
